newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GRABOPLAST BOOSTS PROFITS, SEEKS EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: GRABOPLAST BOOSTS PROFITS, SEEKS EXPANSION.

text.p: Hungarian home improvement product maker Graboplast Rt on Tuesday reported rising profits and sales for the first half of 1997 and said it was planning a capital increase and a further acquisition.
"Graboplast has managed to maintain its long-standing strategic aim to grow in the area of home improvement products, mainly in eastern Europe," Graboplast's CEO Peter Jancso told a news conference.
"Our markets grew faster than our capacity," he added.

Jancso said Graboplast had launched investments of over two billion forints in 1997, most of them aiming at expanding capacity, which would have an impact in the third and fourth quarters of the year.
Graboplast released its first half figures on Tuesday after the close of trading on the Budapest Stock Exchange.

The group reported consolidated operating profits rising to 1.062 billion forints from 719.9 million in the first half of 1996, while its after-tax profit rose to 1.097 billion forints from 423.1 million.
Earnings per share grew to 259 forints from 129, while sales increased to 8.286 billion forints from 6.894 billion.

Jancso said the company planned to invest several billions forints in producing wider PVC floor coverings, and would decide within 60 days whether to do so via an acquisition or a green-field investment.
In order to meet strong demand, Graboplast plans this year to buy a foreign wallpaper factory to add to its 1996 Hungarian acquisition Keszta.
Jancso said the company would raise its capital this year to finance the two projects, subject to shareholders' approval.
He added that Graboplast chose ING Barings as adviser for the equity rise, the size of which he did not disclose.
In the third quarter, traditionally its strongest, Graboplast expects consolidated net sales of 5.943 billion forints and a pre-tax profit of 644 million forints excluding extraordinary items.
